newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors sell WorldCom calls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors sell WorldCom calls.

text.p: Investors were heavy sellers of WorldCom Inc calls Thursday as the stock fell after the company reported second quarter earnings that matched expectations, traders said.
"There's a lot of reaction to the earnings being announced," said an options trader. "They're selling August calls, they're selling September calls and there's offers in December."
The August 35 and September 35 calls were most active, with turnover of 8,370 and 8,375 contracts, respectively.
The August 35 call, which had open interest of 6,873 contracts through Wednesday, was down 5/8 at 7/8.
The September 35 call lost 3/4 to 1-3/4. It had open interest of 11,428 contracts.
By about 1220 CDT/1720 GMT, WorldCom shares were down 7/8 at 35 on turnover of about 11.8 million shares.
The stock fell to a session low of 33-1/2 after it reported a second quarter operating profit of $0.08 per share against $0.25 in the 1996 second quarter.
Analysts' consensus forecast was for the company to earn $0.07 a share in the second quarter, according to First Call.
Traders said that although the earnings beat published estimates, investors were expecting even better numbers from the long distance provider.
"They're just selling volatility," the options trader said of WorldCom options players. "The news event is out and they don't want anything."
Volatilities in the August and September calls near the money were trading around historic levels in the mid-30's, one options dealer said.
In addition to the August and September 35 calls, other active WorldCom calls included the August 32-1/2s, which traded 3,160 and the September 32-1/2s, which traded more than 2,000.
In the December series, the 35 call traded 475 contracts, the 32-1/2 call traded 295 adn the 37-1/2 call traded 180.
The busiest WorldCom put was the August 35, which traded 265 contracts.
